title: Peace between the two is better
hookLine: if a couple fear a rift, reconciliation is best (4:128)

cards: Wa-s-sulhu khayr. In Arabic it's two words, with the and fused onto the first: and reconciliation is better. The phrase sits in a verse about a marriage going cold, but the word reached much further.
Islamic law uses sulh for any settlement that ends a dispute, between neighbors, business partners, or whole families. A word about one marriage is also the word for peace between anyone.
But first, the verse itself, which is surprisingly honest about why making peace is hard.

teach.b: Verse 128 says: if a woman fears ill-treatment or turning away from her husband, there's no sin on them if they settle things between themselves, and reconciliation is better.
Then a surprising line: souls are prone to stinginess.
Shuhh: tight-fistedness, holding on to what you're owed. Each side clutches its rights. Then: if you do good and are mindful of God, God is aware of what you do.
Sulh means settlement, peace-making, a deal that ends a quarrel: the opposite of insisting on every last right.
A'ishah explained the verse, in a report in Sahih al-Bukhari: it's about a husband who no longer wants his wife, and she says, keep me, and I'll give up some of what's due to me.
Each gives something so the bond survives. Commentators connect it to Sawdah, one of the Prophet's wives, who gave her night to A'ishah so the marriage would continue.
Scholars stress that a settlement must be freely chosen, never forced on the weaker side. And the principle spread far beyond marriage. In 49:10: believers are siblings, so make peace between them.
A hadith in Abu Dawud reports the Prophet ﷺ asking: shall I tell you of something better in rank than voluntary fasting, prayer and charity? Setting things right between people.
A hadith in Bukhari even says the one who reconciles people by passing on good words is not a liar.
Reconciliation is better, the verse says. Not easier. Better.

how: Muslims practice sulh, reconciliation, in marriages, families and communities, often through elders or mediators, and Islamic law recognizes settlement as a way to end disputes, provided it is freely agreed.

o: a divorce agreed in front of a judge
a ruling that names who was in the wrong
a settlement where each side gives a little

p: gave her night so the marriage continued

s: it says souls are prone to stinginess: people clutch their rights.
a hadith ranks reconciling people above extra fasting and charity
Abu Dawud reports it: setting things right between people.
scholars allow a settlement to be forced on the weaker side
they stress it must be freely chosen.

games.q: you carry a message between two quarreling friends. you can pass on only the kind things each said. what does the hadith in Bukhari say about that?
o: the one who reconciles people by passing on good is not a liar.
games.why: passing on good words to bring people back together is not counted as lying (Sahih al-Bukhari).

practice: Think of someone close with whom there's distance right now, and name honestly what you're holding on to: the apology you're owed, the point you want conceded.
Then ask what one thing you could let go of, freely, so the bond survives. If you pray, you can ask God to soften both hearts.

wordCard.voice: Sulh. Settlement, reconciliation: each side gives something so the bond survives, from 4:128, and reconciliation is better. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: reconciliation is better. Each side gives a little, and the bond survives. Day three hundred eighty-six, done.
